transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start time: 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Darren Brooks, Anita Rao (Redwood) - Liam O'Connor, Priya Patel, Daniel Wu, Sofia Martinez (EdgeScale)

Summary:
Quick sync on network/routing blockers for Redwood Private VPC pilot; status of runtime/kernel upgrade; perf bench plan and next steps. Some clarity required on egress IPs, firewall rules, and a rollback playbook for kernel/driver updates.

Topics:
- Network & firewall rules (NAT, egress IPs, peering)
- Kernel/driver upgrade for runtime 1.12 and RC patch
- Routing (NAT gateway vs NAT instances, BGP, private link)
- Benchmark results (latency p50/p95/p99) and tuning (batch size, KV cache)
- Security / audit / KMS notes

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, good morning, thanks for joining, think we have the usual crew - hey Liam, Priya, Daniel - thanks for making time. Quick note, we only have 40ish minutes so we'll run through status then blockers.
[00:00:12] Liam O'Connor: Morning Maya, yeah, sounds good. We've got a couple of questions from infra and will want the step by step for the kernel upgrade.
[00:00:20] Darren Brooks: Yeah I'll cover that, we drafted the steps, it's mostly kernel driver bump and NVidia driver compatibility, plus a controlled node reboot sequence. We'll share the playbook after this.
[00:00:35] Priya Patel: Great, we need the exact IPs that Redwood's control plane will talk from so we can add to our firewall allow list - we hit a blocker yesterday where egress got blocked and jobs timed out.
[00:00:48] Anita Rao: To clarify, for Redwood Private (private control plane) the control plane traffic originates from your VPC peered subnets, but there are optional outbound IPs for telemetry when using our managed connectors - I can get that list.
[00:01:05] Sofia Martinez: There's some confusion on peering vs PrivateLink - our security team prefers PrivateLink but we heard PrivateLink isn't fully supported for metrics stream?
[00:01:15] Darren Brooks: Correct, currently metrics streaming for the RC uses a TLS over HTTPS endpoint and we support both peering and PrivateLink, but PrivateLink requires a small network config on your side for endpoint policy, and we need to share the exact hostnames.
[00:01:30] Liam O'Connor: Okay, that's fine, can you send both options, and the security policy we need to apply.
[00:01:38] Maya Chen: Action item noted - Darren/Anita will send network diagram + hostnames.

[00:02:05] Daniel Wu: On the kernel upgrade, we tried the stage yesterday on one node and saw a weird spike in p99 latency for small prompts - maybe related to NVidia driver version mismatch or a thread scheduling change.
[00:02:18] Darren Brooks: That aligns with what we saw in our canary - if the kernel is out of sync with the driver, the batching behavior changes slightly and you can see p99 regressions for short sequences. The mitigation is twofold: ensure the NVidia driver and CUDA toolkit versions match our validated matrix, and apply our runtime 1.12 patch which includes a scheduler fix.
[00:02:40] Priya Patel: Is there a rollback plan if the patch causes disruption? We can't afford long SLO blips.
[00:02:47] Darren Brooks: Yes, we have a rollback: snapshot the node, drain connections, apply patch to one node, run smoke bench, if fail, revert snapshot and restore node. We'll detail exact kubectl/drain/recreate commands in the playbook.
[00:03:05] Liam O'Connor: How long does a node snapshot/rollback take in your tests?
[00:03:10] Darren Brooks: Typically 8-12 minutes to snapshot and restore, plus 3-5 minutes for the node to rejoin, so plan for a 20 minute window worst-case. We'll also show how to fail traffic to dedicated fallback instances during a canary.

[00:04:05] Anita Rao: We also recommend doing the upgrade on a low-traffic shard and running an A/B canary for 10% of requests for 1 hour, check p50/p95/p99 and error rate.
[00:04:18] Priya Patel: That works - one more networking detail: do you need outbound port 443 only, or other ports for KV cache and streaming?
[00:04:27] Anita Rao: Primarily 443, but if you're using our optional prefix KV-sync (for cross-region cache) we may need port 10250 for the agent, though that's optional; most customers keep agent traffic on HTTPS.

[00:05:00] Liam O'Connor: Performance note - after the last tuning we ran, p50 is great (120ms) but p99 hovers around 420ms for our interactive workload. Have you seen much improvement with 1.12 and the scheduler?
[00:05:12] Darren Brooks: Early internal numbers show about 10-15% p99 improvement on short sequences once the driver/kernel are aligned and the scheduler fix is applied - so 420ms could drop to ~360-380ms. But we'll need to re-run your benchmarks with your traffic to be sure.
[00:05:28] Daniel Wu: Are there config knobs we should try pre-upgrade? Batching thresholds? KV cache TTL?
[00:05:36] Anita Rao: Yes, quick wins: reduce max_batch_wait_ms for low-latency services, pin smaller batch sizes for chat endpoints (we recommend 8-16 batch slots for interactive), and enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts - if your workload has many shared prefixes that helps p99 a lot.

[00:06:15] Priya Patel: On quantization: we tested int8 quant on the fp16 model and saw cost benefits but a slight quality dip - is Redwood recommending a mixed profile for inference?
[00:06:25] Darren Brooks: For now, we recommend quantize for non-critical paths or offload background tasks; for interactive production we suggest the new 4-bit profiles only after we review eval sets. We'll send recommended quant profiles per model variant.

[00:07:00] Maya Chen: Quick question on metrics - can you confirm which dashboards you want us to ship to your Grafana? We'll push token-level traces and route-level latency.
[00:07:10] Sofia Martinez: We want token- and route-level latency plus cost per route, and audit logs for all API calls. Also retention needs are 365 days for audit logs.
[00:07:22] Anita Rao: Audit log retention for Private can be configured to 365 days, we have a managed S3 export or a customer-side export - we'll share the instructions.

[00:08:00] Liam O'Connor: Back to the firewall issue - Priya, can you share the firewall error logs? We saw some TLS handshake timeouts in the service logs.
[00:08:08] Priya Patel: Yes I've pasted them in the shared notes, common pattern is TLS handshake fail with ECDHE error, likely due to SNI mismatch when we used an internal proxy.
[00:08:20] Darren Brooks: That matches PrivateLink misconfiguration we've seen; endpoint policy needs the exact hostname and SNI to be allowed. We'll include that in the hostnames doc.

[00:09:30] Anita Rao: On routing choices - if you prefer full VPC peering we recommend static route propagation to avoid asymmetric routing; if you go PrivateLink it's simpler for egress control but you need endpoint policies and potentially an NLB in front.
[00:09:48] Sofia Martinez: Our security team prefers minimal peering and PrivateLink for stricter egress control.
[00:09:55] Maya Chen: Noted - we'll provide both diagrams.

[00:11:00] Daniel Wu: Can we talk about fallback policies? If the pilot cluster faces GPU OOMs or slowdowns, do we have automated fallbacks to a cheaper model or slower path?
[00:11:10] Darren Brooks: Yes, Redwood has smart routing - you can configure fallbacks by latency and error rate to route to a smaller model or pre-warmed CPU path; we'll show a sample routing policy that fails over at p95 > 800ms for 2 minutes.
[00:11:26] Liam O'Connor: Would that cause a quality regression? We need to document what downstream UX looks like.
[00:11:30] Anita Rao: Absolutely, part of the rollout is to define acceptable quality tiers per route. We can attach eval sets to routes and have regression alerts.

[00:12:10] Priya Patel: Regarding the node snapshot, are snapshots stored in our S3 or your managed snapshot service? That affects restore time.
[00:12:18] Darren Brooks: Snapshots are stored in your S3 (we use your KMS for envelope encryption) so restore depends on your S3 throughput, we'll include recommended S3 settings.
[00:13:05] Maya Chen: Quick perf numbers from Redwood bench: after applying the runtime 1.12 RC on our internal canary we saw p99 from 450ms -> 380ms on short prompts, but p50 stayed ~120ms. We'll run the same suite on your sample traffic.
[00:13:23] Anita Rao: Also note disk IO contention can amplify p99s during peak startup; recommend using separate EBS volumes for model cache if possible.

[00:14:00] Daniel Wu: We're running with a NAT gateway in front of our private subnets - will that bottle neck for many small outbound requests?
[00:14:08] Darren Brooks: NAT gateway is fine but watch SNAT port exhaustion with many ephemeral connections; in high throughput cases we suggest using NAT instances with autoscale or put agents behind a shared egress proxy.

[00:15:10] Sofia Martinez: We noticed occasional TLS renegotiation during long streaming sessions; any suggestions?
[00:15:18] Anita Rao: Ensure keepalive settings are long enough and use HTTP/2 streaming where available; also make sure your proxy isn't cutting idle connections aggressively.

[00:16:00] Maya Chen: Let's run through the benchmark plan - we need your sample trace (Liam) and we'll run three passes: baseline (current setup), after kernel/driver alignment, and after runtime tuning (batching/kv). Each pass will include 30-60 minute runs and collect p50/p95/p99 and cost per token.
[00:16:19] Liam O'Connor: We'll share the 12-hour sample overnight, you can start with a 1-hour compressed trace if that helps.
[00:16:28] Anita Rao: That works. Darren will run the bench and annotate config diffs.

[00:17:05] Priya Patel: Security question - KMS integration, will Redwood be using our KMS or your managed KMS? We need to meet our compliance controls.
[00:17:13] Darren Brooks: For Private you can bring your own KMS (BYOK) - our control plane integrates with your KMS via cross-account IAM roles; we'll send the IAM policy snippets.
[00:17:25] Sofia Martinez: Good, we need SOC 2 artifacts and the audit log export details.
[00:17:30] Anita Rao: We'll attach SOC 2 and ISO docs in the security packet; audit exports available as S3 pushes every 24 hours.

[00:18:10] Maya Chen: Anything else on capacity? You mentioned earlier wanting predictable throughput for peak events.
[00:18:16] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, we want a committed baseline for dedicated capacity during our marketing events - will pricing reflect reserved capacity?
[00:18:24] Maya Chen: Yes reserved capacity pricing differs from on-demand; I'll include dedicated monthly commit tiers in the pricing sheet.

[00:19:00] Daniel Wu: One operational ask - we need a playbook for node draining and how to gracefully rehydrate the KV cache to avoid cold starts.
[00:19:07] Darren Brooks: We'll add a cache warmup step to the playbook: pre-populate prefix KV with expected prefixes and pre-warm model shards before traffic.

[00:20:30] Anita Rao: Small note on telemetry: token-level traces can be voluminous - we recommend sampling (1% or route-based sampling) for long-term retention to control cost.
[00:20:42] Priya Patel: OK we'll evaluate sampling.

[00:22:00] Maya Chen: Quick sync on timelines - you aiming for pilot completion by end of August?
[00:22:07] Liam O'Connor: Yes end of August for initial pilot, possibly rolling into a Q4 dedicated capacity purchase.
[00:22:14] Maya Chen: Good, that aligns.

[00:23:00] Darren Brooks: I'll circle back with the kernel upgrade playbook and the exact driver matrix - that should address the p99 regressions you saw.
[00:23:10] Priya Patel: We'd like a dry run of the rollback procedure on a staging node before we touch prod.
[00:23:15] Darren Brooks: Absolutely - we'll schedule the dry run for next week.

[00:24:00] Anita Rao: About the metrics stream to Grafana - do you have a collector? We can send Prometheus exporters or push direct metrics.
[00:24:08] Sofia Martinez: We use hosted Grafana with Prometheus; Prometheus pull is preferred.
[00:24:15] Anita Rao: We'll provide the scrape configs and dashboards.

[00:25:30] Maya Chen: Anything else from EdgeScale?
[00:25:34] Liam O'Connor: Not at the moment, but we'll follow up in the thread with logs and the compressed trace.
[00:25:40] Priya Patel: I'll validate firewall rules tonight and update the ticket.

[00:26:10] Maya Chen: Perfect - recap then next steps.
[00:26:15] Maya Chen: Darren/Anita to send network diagram, hostnames, and kernel upgrade playbook by 2026-07-30. Darren to run dry-run rollback with staging node next week. Liam/Priya to supply sample traffic and firewall logs by 2026-07-31/2026-08-03. Maya to send pricing for dedicated capacity by 2026-08-04. Anita to run benchmark after kernel patch and share results by 2026-07-30.
[00:26:35] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good.
[00:26:40] Daniel Wu: One more small ask - can Redwood provide an example routing policy JSON for failover? We'll use it for our internal runbook.
[00:26:48] Anita Rao: Yes we'll attach an example policy in the follow-up email.

[00:28:00] Maya Chen: Great - we'll send the follow ups. Thanks everyone for the time.
[00:28:06] Liam O'Connor: Thanks, bye.
[00:28:10] Priya Patel: Thanks all, bye.
[00:28:12] Anita Rao: Bye.

End notes:
- Bench plan agreed: 3 passes (baseline, post-driver alignment, post-tuning).
- Primary blockers: firewall allow list (SNI/PrivateLink), kernel/driver mismatch (causing p99 regressions), and cache warmup strategy.
- Follow-ups to include: network diagram + hostnames, kernel upgrade playbook + rollback dry run, sample traffic trace, pricing for dedicated capacity, example routing policy.
